labels.text: Continue previous session, from this device or from your account.

S68.01.needs: a second terminal on this machine; for the cloud part, a signed-in AGI account
S68.01.note: Cloud ids are shown by agi code list; the code gives no other client view of the same id, so only the CLI path was traced.
steps: Start agi in a folder, send one message so the session is saved.
Type /status and note the id on the "Session:" line.
Open a second terminal in the same folder and run agi resume <that id>.
Compare: the second terminal opens the same session id you noted.
S68.01.where: Type /status in the full-screen agi (the same session id is named there); in a second terminal type agi resume <id>

labels.text: Showing the latest turns; earlier turns are not shown.
Continue previous session, from this device or from your account.

S68.02.needs: a second terminal; for the cloud part, a cloud Code session from agi code start
S68.02.note: The cited code line for history moved; the current behaviour is in the cloud show output and resume path.
steps: Start agi, send a message or two, then type /export and note the last exchange.
Open a second terminal and run agi resume <id> for the same session.
Compare the conversation shown there with the one from /export.
For a cloud session run agi code show <id> and compare its turns.
S68.02.where: agi resume <id> in a second terminal; for cloud sessions, agi code show <id>

S68.03.needs: a git checkout; a cloud Code session for the cloud part
steps: Start agi in a git checkout on a branch and type /status.
Note the "Branch:" line.
For a cloud session run agi code list, then agi code show <id>.
Compare the branch shown with the branch the session works on (the "Works on:" line).
S68.03.where: Type /status in agi; for cloud sessions, agi code show <id>

S68.04.needs: a signed-in AGI account with at least one cloud Code session
S68.04.note: This checks the cloud side only; a local terminal session is not shown with a repository line.
steps: Run agi code list in a terminal and note the repository shown for each session.
Run agi code show <id> for one session.
Compare the "Works on:" line with the repository you expect.
S68.04.where: agi code list (then agi code show <id>)

S68.05.needs: a git worktree and a second terminal
steps: Start agi from a git worktree folder and type /status.
Note the "Worktree:" line.
Open another terminal in a different folder and resume the same session with agi resume <id>.
Type /status there and compare its "Worktree:" line; a warning shows if the terminal is in another folder.
S68.05.where: Type /status in agi; /worktree or /wt to change worktree

S68.06.needs: a second terminal resuming the same session
S68.06.note: No single screen compares the two clients; the check needs both terminals.
steps: Start agi and type /model; note the model shown.
Type /memory and note the instruction files it lists.
Repeat in a second terminal with agi resume <id>.
Compare the model and instruction files from both terminals.
S68.06.where: Type /model in agi and /memory in agi

S68.07.needs: a second terminal resuming the same session
steps: Start agi and ask for a multi-step task so a plan appears.
Type /plan show and note the plan steps.
Type /rewind and note the checkpoint list.
Repeat in a second terminal with agi resume <id> and compare the plan and checkpoints.
S68.07.where: Type /plan show in agi, and /rewind for checkpoints

labels.text: Answer with `agi code approve <handle>` or `agi code reject <handle>`.
List the approvals cloud Code sessions are waiting on.

S68.08.needs: a session that asks for an approval; for the cloud part, a cloud Code session waiting on one
S68.08.note: The code shows the approval to a second local terminal is not confirmed; the cross-client view is traced through Remote Control and the cloud approvals.
steps: Start a task in agi that needs a tool approval, and wait for "Waiting for your approval".
Open a second terminal with agi resume <id> and check whether the same approval shows there.
For a cloud session, run agi code approvals and note the handle.
Answer with agi code approve <handle> and check the session shows it answered.
S68.08.where: Local: the "Waiting for your approval" prompt in agi. Cloud: agi code approvals, then agi code approve <handle> or agi code reject <handle>

labels.text: Remote Control hands this session to AGI Mobile

S68.09.needs: AGI Mobile signed in to the same account
S68.09.note: The connected status line says the phone sees tool activity; whether /remote-control is offered in a release build was not checked.
steps: Start agi in full-screen mode and type /remote-control.
Connect AGI Mobile to the same account and open the same session.
Start a task that runs tools and watch the tool activity in agi.
Compare with the tool activity shown in AGI Mobile.
S68.09.where: Type /remote-control in agi (the full-screen interface), with AGI Mobile connected

labels.text: /control release hands it to another client; /control take takes it from whoever is writing it.

S68.12.needs: a second terminal resuming the same session
steps: Start agi on a saved session and type /status.
Note the "Writing:" line that names the client that owns execution.
Type /control and read its status text.
Run agi resume <id> in a second terminal and compare the "Writing:" line in both.
S68.12.where: Type /status in agi; or /control in agi

labels.text: /control release hands it to another client; /control take takes it from whoever is writing it.

S68.13.needs: a second terminal writing the same session
steps: Start agi on a session that another terminal is writing.
Type /control and read who is writing it.
Type /control take in this terminal.
Check the reply "This terminal now writes session" and check the other terminal's status says it stopped writing.
S68.13.where: Type /control release or /control take in agi

labels.text: Hand this session to the cloud?
Continue a local session in a new cloud Code session: its objective,

S68.16.needs: a GitHub checkout with a pushed branch, a signed-in account and a local session
S68.16.note: There is no /handoff slash command in the code; the handoff is a CLI command.
steps: In a GitHub checkout with a pushed branch, run agi code handoff.
Read the review text shown before the prompt.
At "Hand this session to the cloud?" answer n to cancel, or y to hand it over.
Check the output: the session appears in agi code list.
S68.16.where: agi code handoff (in a git checkout); or agi code start "<task>"

labels.text: Hand this session to the cloud?

S68.18.needs: a GitHub checkout with a pushed branch and a signed-in account
steps: Run agi code handoff without --yes in a GitHub checkout.
Read the section "What moves to the cloud".
Read the section "What stays on this machine" and the "Access:" line.
At "Hand this session to the cloud?" answer n to stop without a transfer.
S68.18.where: agi code handoff (read the review before answering the prompt)

labels.text: List the devices signed in to your AGI account, whether each

S68.21.needs: a signed-in AGI account with at least one device
S68.21.note: The host list in the code covers local models, local MCP servers, a browser, computer use and remote control; code sessions are not in it.
steps: Run agi devices in a terminal.
Read the "Your devices" list and each line's "can host" part.
Compare with the devices you signed in on (local models, browser, MCP, computer use, remote control).
Check that a device which reports nothing shows "reports nothing it can host".

S68.26.needs: a way to drop the network connection, and AGI Mobile connected
S68.26.note: The code shows the reconnecting status, not the resume of state itself; whether the state resumes was not traced.
steps: Start agi in full-screen mode, connect Remote Control with /remote-control.
Turn off the network for a short time, then turn it back on.
Watch the status line for "Remote Control: reconnecting".
Check the session continues with the same conversation after reconnecting.
S68.26.where: Type /remote-control in agi, then watch the status line for "Remote Control: reconnecting"

S68.27.note: Context is written only as the transcript format chosen; the export formats are json, answer and markdown (md).
steps: Start agi, send a message, and type /export to see the transcript shown on screen.
Type /export json followed by a file path ending in .json, for example ~/Desktop/session.json.
Open the file and check it holds the transcript.
Note that a relative path is saved under the workspace folder.
S68.27.where: Type /export in agi (add a path such as /export json ~/Desktop/session.json to write a file)
